questions.prompt: Is it important for children to play sports?

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Importance of Sports for Children
phrases: manage winning and losing with grace
sentenceStarters: Yes, I think sports participation is genuinely important for children...
But I think the non-physical benefits of sports are equally significant...
I also think sports provide children with a domain...

questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I think it's good. Good for health. Children can run around. It's important. But, um, maybe not all the time because school is also important.
questions.sampleBand6: Um, yes, I think it's important. Children need to let off steam, you know? And sports are a good way to do that. Also, it teaches them about teamwork and, um, being competitive. But, I guess, it's not the only important thing.
questions.sampleBand7: Yes, I definitely think it's important. Firstly, it's crucial for their physical health; it helps them stay in shape and develop good habits early on. Moreover, sports can teach them valuable life skills, like teamwork and discipline. Taking part in sports is really beneficial, I think.
questions.sampleBand8: Absolutely, I believe sports are essential for children. Not only do they promote physical well-being and help ward off childhood obesity, but they also play a vital role in their social and emotional development. Learning to cooperate as part of a team, handle both success and failure, and develop resilience are all incredibly valuable life lessons that sports can impart. It's particularly important in today's screen-dominated world.
questions.sampleBand9: Without a doubt, sports are incredibly important for children. It's not just about the physical benefits, although those are undeniable – fostering healthy habits early on can set them up for life. But beyond that, participation in sports cultivates essential character traits. Kids learn teamwork, discipline, and how to bounce back from setbacks. They also develop leadership skills and learn to manage their time effectively. Ultimately, sports offer a holistic learning experience that complements academic pursuits and prepares them to face the world with confidence.
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think sports participation is genuinely important for children, and the benefits extend well beyond the obvious physical health dimension. The physical benefits are real and significant—regular physical activity during childhood establishes habits and physiological patterns that have long-term health consequences, and the rates of childhood obesity and sedentary behaviour in many countries make this more important than ever. But I think the non-physical benefits of sports are equally significant and perhaps less widely appreciated. Team sports in particular develop a range of social and emotional competencies—the ability to cooperate toward a shared goal, to manage both winning and losing with grace, to support teammates, to accept coaching and criticism, and to understand that individual performance is embedded in a collective context. These are qualities that are genuinely valuable in adult life and that are difficult to develop in purely academic settings. I also think sports provide children with a domain in which effort and improvement are directly visible and rewarding—where the connection between practice and progress is clear and motivating—which can be a powerful source of confidence and self-efficacy that transfers to other areas of life.

Ammo bundan tashqari, sportda ishtirok etish muhim xarakter xususiyatlarini rivojlantiradi. Bolalar jamoada ishlashni, intizomni va qanday qilib qiyinchiliklardan so'ng tiklanishni o'rganadilar. Ular, shuningdek, yetakchilik ko'nikmalarini rivojlantiradilar va vaqtlarini samarali boshqarishni o'rganadilar. Oxir oqibat, sport akademik mashg'ulotlarni to'ldiradigan va ularni ishonch bilan dunyoga yuz tutishga tayyorlaydigan yaxlit o'rganish tajribasini taklif etadi.

Ammo men sportning jismoniy bo'lmagan foydalari ham shunchalik muhim va ehtimol kamroq qadrlanadi deb o'ylayman. Ayniqsa, jamoaviy sport turlari bir qator ijtimoiy va hissiy kompetensiyalarni rivojlantiradi - umumiy maqsadga erishish uchun hamkorlik qilish qobiliyati, g'alaba va mag'lubiyatni odob bilan boshqarish, jamoadoshlarni qo'llab-quvvatlash, murabbiylik va tanqidni qabul qilish va individual ko'rsatkichlar kollektiv kontekstga bog'liqligini tushunish. Bular kattalar hayotida haqiqatan ham qimmatli bo'lgan va faqat akademik muhitda rivojlantirish qiyin bo'lgan fazilatlar. Men, shuningdek, sport bolalarga harakat va yaxshilanish to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ko'rinadigan va rag'batlantiruvchi sohani taqdim etadi deb o'ylayman - amaliyot va taraqqiyot o'rtasidagi bog'liqlik aniq va rag'batlantiruvchi - bu hayotning boshqa sohalariga o'tadigan ishonch va o'ziga ishonchning kuchli manbai bo'lishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Do you think people do enough sport these days?

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do People Do Enough Sport
phrases: designed physical activity out of everyday life
separate decision to go to the gym
sentenceStarters: No, I don't think most people do enough physical activity...
The structural conditions of modern life work against physical activity...
I also think there's a significant inequality dimension...

While some people are on the ball about fitness, I think the majority could definitely benefit from upping their activity levels. questions.sampleBand9: No, I don't believe the average person gets sufficient exercise. We've created a society where convenience often takes precedence over health. While there's certainly a growing trend toward wellness, overall, people are still falling short. It's a complex issue, of course, with factors like time constraints, financial limitations, and simply a lack of motivation playing a part. To really move the needle, we need to foster a culture where physical activity is seamlessly integrated into daily life, rather than seen as an optional extra.
questions.sampleAnswer: No, I don't think most people do enough physical activity, and the evidence from public health research is fairly unambiguous on this point—rates of physical inactivity are high in most developed countries, and the health consequences are significant. The structural conditions of modern life work against physical activity in ways that make it genuinely difficult for many people to be as active as they should be—sedentary office work, long commutes, the convenience of cars, and the appeal of screen-based leisure all reduce the amount of movement in daily life. I think the problem is partly that we've designed physical activity out of everyday life and then expect people to add it back in as a deliberate, time-consuming extra. The most effective approaches to increasing physical activity are probably those that integrate movement into daily routines—active commuting, walkable urban design, standing desks—rather than those that rely on people making a separate decision to go to the gym. I also think there's a significant inequality dimension—access to sports facilities, safe outdoor spaces, and leisure time is not equally distributed, and the people who are least physically active are often those with the fewest resources and the most constrained lives.

questions.uzSampleBand8: Men odamlar yetarli darajada qilyapti deb aytmayman, yo'q. Umuman olganda, menimcha, zamonaviy turmush tarzi tobora harakatsiz bo'lib bormoqda. Ba'zi odamlar fitnesga e'tiborli bo'lsa-da, menimcha, ko'pchilik o'z faollik darajasini oshirishdan foyda olishi mumkin. Bu haqiqiy ijtimoiy muammo, ayniqsa stol ishlarining ko'payishi bilan.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Yo'q, men o'rtacha odam yetarli darajada mashq qiladi deb o'ylamayman. Biz qulaylik ko'pincha sog'liqdan ustun turadigan jamiyatni yaratdik. Bu, albatta, murakkab masala, vaqt cheklovlari, moliyaviy cheklovlar va shunchaki motivatsiyaning yo'qligi kabi omillar o'z rolini o'ynaydi. Haqiqatan ham o'zgarish qilish uchun biz jismoniy faollikni majburiy qo'shimcha sifatida emas, balki kundalik hayotga uzviy ravishda integratsiya qilingan madaniyatni rivojlantirishimiz kerak.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Yo'q, menimcha, ko'pchilik jismoniy faollik bilan yetarli darajada shug'ullanmaydi va bu borada jamoat salomatligi tadqiqotlarining dalillari ancha aniq - ko'pgina rivojlangan mamlakatlarda jismoniy harakatsizlik darajasi yuqori va sog'liq uchun oqibatlari sezilarli. Menimcha, muammo qisman shundaki, biz jismoniy faollikni kundalik hayotdan chiqarib tashladik va keyin odamlardan uni ataylab, vaqt talab qiladigan qo'shimcha sifatida qaytarishni kutamiz. questions.prompt: How do people in your country stay fit?

vocabulary.title: Q3 - How People Stay Fit
sentenceStarters: People in my country stay fit through a fairly diverse range...
Gym membership has grown substantially...
I think there's also been a significant growth in home-based fitness...

questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I think some people go to the gym. And, uh, others, they play football sometimes. It's, uh, quite popular, I think. But, yeah, not everyone does it.
questions.sampleBand6: Um, well, there are a few ways. Actually, many people take up jogging or running, especially in the parks. Others join a gym, but I think it's more common to see people walking. It's quite a walking culture, I'd say, really.
questions.sampleBand7: Well, generally, people in my country try to stay fit in a variety of ways. A lot of people go in for team sports like football or basketball. Others prefer individual activities like running or swimming. And of course, many people attend fitness classes at local gyms. It really depends on their personal preferences and what's easily accessible to them.
questions.sampleBand8: Well, there's quite a range of approaches, honestly. Many people are getting into things like yoga and Pilates, which are becoming increasingly popular. Of course, traditional sports like football remain very popular, especially amongst younger people. And with the growing awareness of health, more people are consciously trying to incorporate exercise into their daily routines, like walking or cycling to work. It's definitely becoming more of a priority for many.
questions.sampleBand9: Well, it's interesting because there's a real mix of approaches. On the one hand, you have the traditional sports like football and basketball that are still incredibly popular, particularly among younger generations. But increasingly, there's a focus on holistic well-being, with people taking up activities like yoga and mindfulness. Plus, the government has been actively promoting initiatives to encourage people to lead a healthy lifestyle, such as building more cycle lanes and pedestrian areas. So, it’s becoming easier for people to fit exercise in to their daily routines, and I think that’s making a real difference in the long run.
questions.sampleAnswer: People in my country stay fit through a fairly diverse range of activities, and I think the picture has changed significantly over the past couple of decades as both the options available and the cultural attitudes toward fitness have evolved. Gym membership has grown substantially—fitness centres are now much more widespread and accessible than they were a generation ago, and the range of classes and activities they offer has expanded considerably. Running has become enormously popular—the growth of parkrun, marathon participation, and recreational running more generally has been remarkable. Cycling has also grown significantly, partly driven by investment in cycling infrastructure and partly by a growing environmental consciousness. Team sports—football, rugby, cricket, netball—continue to have large participation numbers, particularly among younger people. Walking remains the most widely practised form of physical activity across all age groups—it's accessible, free, and can be integrated into daily routines in ways that more structured exercise cannot. I think there's also been a significant growth in home-based fitness—yoga, pilates, and online workout programmes have made it possible for people to exercise without leaving their homes, which has expanded access for people who find gyms intimidating or who have time constraints.

questions.sampleAnswer: The sports that children do at school vary significantly by country, region, and the type of school, but there are some fairly consistent patterns. In my country, team ball sports are the most common—football, rugby, cricket, and netball are staples of the school sports curriculum, and most schools have facilities for at least some of these. Athletics—running, jumping, and throwing events—is also a standard part of the curriculum, typically organised around an annual sports day that many children remember as a significant event. Swimming is taught in many schools, particularly at primary level, and is considered an important life skill rather than simply a sport. Gymnastics and dance are also common, particularly in primary schools. I think the range of sports available at school has an important influence on children's long-term relationship with physical activity—children who discover a sport they enjoy at school are more likely to continue being active into adulthood. The challenge is that the traditional school sports curriculum tends to favour competitive team sports, which suits some children but not others, and there's a growing recognition that offering a wider range of activities—including individual sports, outdoor pursuits, and non-competitive movement—would engage a broader range of children.

questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, the internet has transformed the possibilities for self-directed learning in ways that are genuinely remarkable, and I think it's one of the most significant educational developments of the past few decades. The most obvious benefit is access to information—the internet has made an extraordinary range of knowledge available to anyone with a connection, which has democratised access to learning in ways that were previously impossible. A student in a remote area with limited library resources now has access to the same information as a student at a well-resourced university. Beyond information access, the internet has enabled new forms of learning—online courses, educational videos, interactive simulations, and collaborative platforms have created learning experiences that are more engaging and more flexible than traditional classroom instruction. I also think the internet is particularly valuable for self-directed learners who want to go beyond the curriculum—to explore topics in greater depth, to find alternative explanations, or to connect with communities of people who share their interests. The challenge is that the internet also contains a great deal of unreliable information, and developing the critical thinking skills to evaluate sources and distinguish reliable from unreliable information is an increasingly important educational goal.

questions.sampleBand9: Yes, there are undoubtedly some inherent risks involved. One significant danger is the vulnerability to online fraud and identity theft; it's remarkably easy for unscrupulous individuals to get hold of your financial details. Furthermore, the lack of physical inspection before purchase means you're essentially buying a pig in a poke. The item might not match the description, or the quality could be substandard. And finally, navigating the returns process, customer service, and potential disputes can be a frustrating and time-consuming ordeal, making it a double-edged sword.
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, there are genuine risks associated with online shopping, and I think it's important to be aware of them even if the overall experience of online shopping is generally safe and positive. The most significant risk is probably fraud and scams—the internet has created new opportunities for criminals to deceive consumers, whether through fake websites that mimic legitimate retailers, phishing emails that attempt to steal payment information, or counterfeit products sold as genuine. The risk of data breaches is also real—when you make a purchase online, you share personal and financial information with the retailer, and if that retailer's systems are compromised, your data can be exposed. I think the practical response to these risks is to develop good habits—shopping only from reputable retailers, checking that websites use secure connections, using payment methods that offer buyer protection, and being sceptical of deals that seem too good to be true. There are also less dramatic but still significant risks—the difficulty of assessing quality before purchase, the inconvenience of returns, and the environmental cost of packaging and delivery. I also think there's a broader risk associated with the concentration of online retail in a small number of very large platforms, which raises questions about market power, worker conditions, and the long-term health of diverse retail ecosystems.

They're more likely to use phones for social media, streaming, gaming, and content creation, and they tend to communicate through messaging apps and visual platforms rather than voice calls. Older users tend to have a more instrumental relationship with their phones—using them for specific purposes like calls, messages, navigation, and information lookup—and are generally less immersed in the social and entertainment dimensions of smartphone use. They're also more likely to use voice calls as their primary mode of communication. questions.prompt: What positive and negative effects do mobile phones have on friendship?

vocabulary.title: Q12 - Phones and Friendship
phrases: send a message or share a photo
sentenceStarters: Mobile phones have had genuinely complex effects on friendship...

questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I think, on the one hand, it's easier to keep up with friends. But, um, sometimes people are always on their phones and don't talk face to face. So, yeah, maybe that's bad.
questions.sampleBand6: I mean, there are definitely both positive and negative sides. Positively, it's much easier to stay in touch, especially if friends move away. questions.sampleBand7: Mobile phones have undeniable benefits for friendships. It's easier than ever to coordinate plans, share experiences instantly, and check in on friends who might be struggling. However, there's a downside. People can become glued to their screens, neglecting real-life interactions, and misinterpretations can arise more easily through text messages.
questions.sampleBand8: Well, it's a double-edged sword, isn't it? On the one hand, mobile phones facilitate constant connection. We can share photos, videos, and organise social events really easily. It's great for maintaining long-distance friendships. On the other hand, relying on digital communication can lead to a decline in the quality of face-to-face interactions. People might feel more comfortable hiding behind a screen, which can take a toll on genuine emotional connection.
questions.sampleBand9: Mobile phones have profoundly reshaped the landscape of friendship, offering both unprecedented opportunities and potential pitfalls. Undoubtedly, they foster a sense of instantaneous connection, allowing us to share moments and support each other regardless of geographical distance. We can nip problems in the bud. However, the constant accessibility can also be detrimental. The curated reality presented on social media can breed envy and insecurity, and the sheer volume of digital communication can overshadow the depth and authenticity of real-life interactions. It's about finding a happy medium, I suppose.
questions.sampleAnswer: Mobile phones have had genuinely complex effects on friendship—they've made some aspects of friendship easier and more continuous while potentially undermining others. On the positive side, phones have made it much easier to maintain friendships across distance and time—the ability to send a message, share a photo, or make a video call at any moment means that friendships that would previously have faded due to geographical separation can now be maintained with much less effort. Group messaging apps have also created new forms of social connection—the ability to maintain a continuous conversation with a group of friends, to share experiences in real time, and to coordinate social activities has genuine value. On the negative side, I think there are real concerns about the quality of phone-mediated connection compared to face-to-face interaction. The research suggests that in-person interaction is more emotionally rich and more conducive to the kind of deep connection that characterises genuine friendship, and that the convenience of digital communication can sometimes substitute for rather than supplement face-to-face time. There's also the issue of phone use during social gatherings—the habit of checking phones while in the company of others is widely recognised as damaging to the quality of social interaction and as a form of disrespect to the people you're with. I think the most important thing is to use phones in ways that enhance rather than replace genuine human connection.
questions.uzSampleBand5: Xo'sh, um, menimcha, bir tomondan, do'stlar bilan aloqada bo'lib turish osonroq. Lekin, um, ba'zida odamlar doim telefonlarida bo'lishadi va yuzma-yuz gaplashishmaydi. Shunday qilib, ha, ehtimol, bu yomon.

Biroq, salbiy tomoni shundaki, odamlar faqat onlayn muloqot qilishlari sababli, real hayotda uzoqlaishib ketishlari mumkin. Bu biroz yuzaki bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleBand7: Mobil telefonlarning do'stlik uchun inkor etib bo'lmaydigan foydalari bor. Odamlar ekranlariga mixlanib qolishlari, real hayotdagi muloqotlarni e'tiborsiz qoldirishlari mumkin va matnli xabarlar orqali noto'g'ri talqinlar osonroq paydo bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Xo'sh, bu ikki tig'li qilich, shunday emasmi? Bir tomondan, mobil telefonlar doimiy aloqani osonlashtiradi. Biz fotosuratlar, videolar bilan bo'lishishimiz va ijtimoiy tadbirlarni tashkil qilishimiz juda oson. Bu uzoq masofadagi do'stlikni saqlab qolish uchun ajoyib. questions.uzSampleBand9: Mobil telefonlar do'stlik manzarasini tubdan o'zgartirdi, ular misli ko'rilmagan imkoniyatlar va potentsial xavflarni taklif qilmoqda. Biz muammolarni ildizidan bartaraf etishimiz mumkin. Biroq, doimiy mavjudlik ham zararli bo'lishi mumkin. questions.uzSampleAnswer: Mobil telefonlar do'stlikka chinakam murakkab ta'sir ko'rsatdi—ular do'stlikning ba'zi jihatlarini osonlashtirdi va uzluksiz qildi, shu bilan birga boshqalariga putur yetkazishi mumkin. Ijobiy tomoni shundaki, telefonlar masofa va vaqt bo'yicha do'stlikni saqlab qolishni ancha osonlashtirdi—istalgan vaqtda xabar yuborish, rasm ulashish yoki video qo'ng'iroq qilish imkoniyati geografik ajralish tufayli avval yo'qolib ketgan do'stliklarni endi kamroq harakat bilan saqlab qolish mumkin degani. Guruhli xabar almashish ilovalari ham ijtimoiy aloqaning yangi shakllarini yaratdi—do'stlar guruhi bilan doimiy suhbatni davom ettirish, tajribalarni real vaqtda ulashish va ijtimoiy tadbirlarni muvofiqlashtirish imkoniyati haqiqiy ahamiyatga ega. Salbiy tomoni shundaki, telefon orqali o'rnatilgan aloqaning yuzma-yuz muloqotga nisbatan sifati haqida jiddiy xavotirlar bor deb o'ylayman. Tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, shaxsiy muloqot emotsional jihatdan boyroq va haqiqiy do'stlikka xos bo'lgan chuqur aloqa uchun ko'proq qulaydir va raqamli aloqaning qulayligi ba'zan yuzma-yuz vaqtni to'ldirish o'rniga almashtirishi mumkin. Menimcha, eng muhimi, telefonlardan haqiqiy insoniy aloqani almashtirish o'rniga yaxshilaydigan tarzda foydalanish kerak.

If you're constantly glued to your phone, trying to document every single thing, then you're probably missing out on actually experiencing life. That said, photography is a powerful tool for preserving memories and sharing experiences, so it's all about finding a balance. It really depends on the individual and how they use it.
questions.sampleBand9: That's an interesting point. I don't believe it's a black and white issue. While excessive phone photography can certainly detract from living in the moment, turning experiences into a superficial quest for the perfect Instagram post, it also offers incredible opportunities. We can now document and share our lives with ease, creating lasting memories and even using photography as a form of artistic expression. It really boils down to intention and moderation. If approached mindfully, phone photography can undoubtedly enrich our lives; however, if it becomes an obsession, it might be time to re-evaluate our priorities and strike a balance.
questions.sampleAnswer: I don't think taking pictures with phones is inherently a waste of time, but I do think there are ways of doing it that are counterproductive and that deserve some critical reflection. The most obvious concern is the phenomenon sometimes called 'photo-taking impairment'—the research finding that taking a photo of something can actually reduce your memory of the experience, because the act of photographing substitutes for the deeper processing that creates lasting memories. If you spend a significant portion of an experience looking at it through a screen rather than engaging with it directly, you may end up with a record of the experience but a diminished experience of it. I think this is a real risk, particularly at significant moments—concerts, travel, family gatherings—where the temptation to document is strong. However, I also think photography has genuine value—it's a creative practice, it creates records that have real meaning over time, and the ability to share experiences with people who weren't present has genuine social value. The question is whether you're using photography to enhance your engagement with an experience or to substitute for it. I think the most honest answer is that it depends entirely on how you do it—a few thoughtful photos that capture something genuine are very different from compulsive documentation that keeps you at a remove from what's actually happening.

questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think most people have a fairly extensive list of ways in which mobile phones—or more precisely, other people's use of mobile phones—can be genuinely annoying, and I think this reflects some real tensions between individual behaviour and social norms that are still being worked out. The most universally recognised example is probably phone use during conversations—the experience of talking to someone who is simultaneously checking their phone is almost universally experienced as disrespectful and dismissive, and yet it's extremely common. Loud phone calls in public spaces—on trains, in restaurants, in waiting rooms—are another common source of irritation, particularly when the conversation is personal or conducted at a volume that makes it impossible to ignore. Phones ringing at inappropriate moments—during performances, in meetings, in quiet spaces—is a related annoyance that most people have experienced. The use of phones at the dinner table, particularly in family settings, is a source of significant tension in many households. I also think the more subtle forms of phone-related annoyance are worth mentioning—the person who is physically present but mentally elsewhere because they're absorbed in their phone, the constant notification sounds that punctuate shared spaces, and the social pressure to respond immediately to messages that can make people feel perpetually on call.

Kechki ovqat stolida, ayniqsa oilaviy muhitda telefonlardan foydalanish ko'plab xonadonlarda jiddiy ziddiyat manbai hisoblanadi. Menimcha, telefon bilan bog'liq g'azabning yanada nozik shakllarini ham eslatib o'tishga arziydi - jismonan shu yerda bo'lgan, lekin telefonga berilib ketgani uchun ruhiy jihatdan boshqa joyda bo'lgan odam, umumiy joylarni ajratib turadigan doimiy bildirishnoma tovushlari va odamlarni doimo aloqada bo'lishga majbur qiladigan xabarlarga zudlik bilan javob berish uchun ijtimoiy bosim.

questions.prompt: Do you think there should be laws on the use of mobile phones?

vocabulary.title: Q15 - Laws on Mobile Phone Use
phrases: laws against handheld phone while driving
restricting phone use in certain contexts
broader legal restrictions in public spaces
meaningful control over attention and data
sentenceStarters: Yes, I think some legal regulation of mobile phone use is justified...
Beyond driving, I think the case for legal regulation becomes more complex...
I do think there's a strong case for regulatory intervention in the design...

questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I think maybe there should be some rules. Because, um, people, you know, drive cars and text. It's bad. It can cause problems. Yeah.
questions.sampleBand6: I think that, definitely, there should be some laws about using mobile phones. I mean, it can be really dangerous, particularly when people are driving. Some people get distracted and it can cause accidents. However, it's difficult to enforce these laws.
questions.sampleBand7: I believe that regulations regarding mobile phone use are probably necessary. Driving while using a phone is a clear danger, and stricter laws could help to deter people. Furthermore, in certain public spaces, like libraries or theatres, designated 'phone-free' zones, enforced by law, could improve the experience for everyone.
questions.sampleBand8: That's an interesting question. I'd say yes, there's a strong argument for having laws about mobile phone usage, particularly in situations where safety is paramount. Driving is the obvious example, but also perhaps in places like hospitals where phone use can cause interference with medical equipment. It's a tricky balance though; we don't want to go overboard and restrict people's freedoms unnecessarily, but a sensible framework seems justified.
questions.sampleBand9: I think a nuanced approach is required. Absolutely, there's a case for legislation in specific contexts. For instance, driving while using a mobile phone is demonstrably dangerous, and robust laws are essential to deter such behaviour. On the other hand, a blanket ban on mobile phone use would be impractical and a step too far. The key is to identify situations where mobile phone use poses a significant risk or infringes upon the rights of others, and then implement targeted regulations. It's about striking a balance between public safety and individual liberty, and finding a way to promote responsible usage.
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think some legal regulation of mobile phone use is justified and already exists in many countries—the most obvious example being laws against using a handheld phone while driving, which are well-established and widely accepted as necessary for road safety. The evidence that phone use while driving significantly increases the risk of accidents is unambiguous, and the case for legal prohibition is straightforward. Beyond driving, I think the case for legal regulation becomes more complex and more contested. There are good arguments for restricting phone use in certain contexts—schools, hospitals, courtrooms—where the disruption or privacy implications are significant, and many of these restrictions already exist in various forms. I'm more sceptical about broader legal restrictions on phone use in public spaces—I think social norms and individual responsibility are better mechanisms than law for addressing most forms of phone-related rudeness or distraction. I do think there's a strong case for regulatory intervention in the design of phones and apps—requiring transparency about addictive design features, restricting certain practices that target children, and giving users more meaningful control over their own attention and data. This kind of regulation addresses the structural causes of problematic phone use rather than simply penalising individual behaviour.

questions.uzSampleBand6: Menimcha, albatta, mobil telefonlardan foydalanish haqida qonunlar bo'lishi kerak. Aytmoqchimanki, bu juda xavfli bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa odamlar mashina haydashayotganda. Ba'zi odamlar chalg'iydi va bu baxtsiz hodisalarga olib kelishi mumkin. Biroq, bu qonunlarni amalga oshirish qiyin.
questions.uzSampleBand7: Menimcha, mobil telefonlardan foydalanish bo'yicha qoidalar ehtimol zarurdir. Telefondan foydalangan holda haydash aniq xavfdir va qat'iyroq qonunlar odamlarni to'xtatishga yordam berishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ba'zi jamoat joylarida, masalan, kutubxonalar yoki teatrlarda, qonun bilan ta'minlangan 'telefonsiz' zonalar, hamma uchun tajribani yaxshilashi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Bu qiziqarli savol. Men ha deb aytardim, mobil telefonlardan foydalanish haqida qonunlar bo'lishi uchun kuchli asos bor, ayniqsa xavfsizlik birinchi o'rinda turadigan vaziyatlarda. Haydash - bu aniq misol, lekin, ehtimol, kasalxonalar kabi joylarda ham telefonlardan foydalanish tibbiy uskunalar bilan aralashuvga olib kelishi mumkin. Bu murakkab muvozanat, garchi biz chegaradan o'tib ketmoqchi emasmiz va odamlarning erkinliklarini keraksiz cheklamoqchi emasmiz, lekin oqilona asos o'rinli ko'rinadi.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Menimcha, nozik yondashuv talab etiladi. Albatta, muayyan kontekstlarda qonunchilik uchun asos bor. Misol uchun, mobil telefondan foydalangan holda haydash aniq xavfli va bunday xatti-harakatlarni to'xtatish uchun kuchli qonunlar zarur. Boshqa tomondan, mobil telefonlardan foydalanishga umumiy taqiq amaliy bo'lmaydi va haddan tashqari qadam bo'ladi. Asosiysi, mobil telefondan foydalanish sezilarli xavf tug'diradigan yoki boshqalarning huquqlarini buzadigan vaziyatlarni aniqlash va keyin maqsadli qoidalarni amalga oshirish. Bu jamoat xavfsizligi va shaxsiy erkinlik o'rtasida muvozanatni saqlash va mas'uliyatli foydalanishni rag'batlantirish yo'lini topish haqida.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Ha, menimcha, mobil telefonlardan foydalanishni qonuniy tartibga solish o'rinli va ko'plab mamlakatlarda allaqachon mavjud—buning eng aniq misoli haydash paytida qo'lda telefon ishlatishga qarshi qonunlardir, ular yaxshi o'rnatilgan va yo'l xavfsizligi uchun zarur deb keng qabul qilingan. Haydash paytida telefondan foydalanish baxtsiz hodisalarni xavfini sezilarli darajada oshirishi haqidagi dalillar aniq va qonuniy taqiqlash uchun asos to'g'ridan-to'g'ri. Haydashdan tashqari, menimcha, qonuniy tartibga solish uchun asos yanada murakkab va bahsli bo'lib qoladi. Ma'lum kontekstlarda—maktablar, kasalxonalar, sud zallarida—telefonlardan foydalanishni cheklash uchun yaxshi dalillar bor, bu yerda buzilish yoki maxfiylik oqibatlari sezilarli va bu cheklovlarning ko'pchiligi allaqachon turli shakllarda mavjud. Men jamoat joylarida telefondan foydalanishga kengroq qonuniy cheklovlar haqida ko'proq shubhada bo'laman—menimcha, ijtimoiy me'yorlar va shaxsiy mas'uliyat telefon bilan bog'liq qo'pollik yoki chalg'itishning ko'p shakllarini hal qilish uchun qonundan ko'ra yaxshiroq mexanizmlardir. Men telefonlar va ilovalarning dizayniga tartibga soluvchi aralashuv uchun kuchli asos bor deb o'ylayman—odatlantiruvchi dizayn xususiyatlari haqida shaffoflikni talab qilish, bolalarni nishonga oladigan ma'lum amaliyotlarni cheklash va foydalanuvchilarga o'z e'tibori va ma'lumotlarini yanada mazmunli nazorat qilish imkoniyatini berish. Ushbu turdagi tartibga solish shunchaki individual xatti-harakatni jazolash o'rniga, muammoli telefon foydalanishining tarkibiy sabablarini hal qiladi.

questions.prompt: How have mobile phones changed the way we communicate?

vocabulary.title: Q16 - How Phones Changed Communication
phrases: both parties available at same time
text voice video image and emoji
sentenceStarters: Mobile phones have transformed communication in ways that are so pervasive...
The most fundamental change is probably the shift from synchronous to asynchronous...
I think one of the most significant changes is the blurring of the boundary...

questions.sampleBand5: Well, basically, I think it's easier to talk to people now. You can get in touch fast. Um, send messages is very easy. It's, um, good for that.
questions.sampleBand6: I mean, mobile phones have definitely changed things. It's much easier to keep in touch with people who live far away. Actually, you don't even need to call; you can just text. Sometimes people rely on it too much, though, and forget how to talk face-to-face.
questions.sampleBand7: Mobile phones have, undoubtedly, revolutionised communication. It's now incredibly easy to reach out to someone, regardless of their location. We can send emails, text, or video call. Furthermore, this has also led to a decline in face-to-face interactions, which is a real shame. People sometimes forget how to communicate in person.
questions.sampleBand8: Well, mobile phones have fundamentally altered the way we communicate. It's certainly made communication more accessible and immediate. We can get hold of people instantly, practically anywhere in the world. Moreover, it's not just about calls anymore; we have social media, messaging apps, and video conferencing. However, this ease of communication also has its downsides, leading to a potential lack of depth in our interactions, I think.
questions.sampleBand9: Mobile phones have unquestionably transformed communication, creating a hyper-connected world. The immediacy and accessibility they offer are unprecedented; we can get in contact with anyone, anywhere, at any time. This has fostered global collaboration and broken down barriers. Furthermore, the sheer variety of communication methods – from instant messaging to video calls – is staggering. However, this constant connectivity can be a double-edged sword, potentially leading to superficial relationships and a blurring of boundaries between work and personal life; we need to strike a balance, I think.
questions.sampleAnswer: Mobile phones—and particularly smartphones—have transformed communication in ways that are so pervasive that it's now difficult to remember what communication looked like before them. The most fundamental change is probably the shift from synchronous to asynchronous communication as the default mode—before mobile phones, most communication was either face-to-face or by phone call, both of which require both parties to be available at the same time. Messaging has made it normal to communicate in a way that doesn't require immediate response, which has both advantages—you can communicate at your own pace, across time zones, without interrupting what you're doing—and disadvantages—the expectation of availability has in some ways increased rather than decreased, and many people feel a pressure to respond quickly that can be genuinely stressful. The range of communication modes available has also expanded dramatically—text, voice, video, image, and emoji all serve different communicative functions and have created new forms of expression. I think one of the most significant changes is the blurring of the boundary between public and private communication—the ease with which messages can be shared, forwarded, and broadcast has changed the nature of private conversation in ways that have significant implications for trust and intimacy. The permanence of digital communication—the fact that messages can be stored, searched, and retrieved—is also a significant change from the ephemeral nature of spoken conversation.
questions.uzSampleBand5: Xo'sh, aslida, menimcha, hozir odamlar bilan gaplashish osonroq. Siz tezda bog'lana olasiz. Um, xabar yuborish juda oson. Bu, um, shu uchun yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleBand6: Menimcha, mobil telefonlar albatta narsalarni o'zgartirdi. Uzoqda yashaydigan odamlar bilan aloqada bo'lish ancha oson. Aslida, qo'ng'iroq qilish ham shart emas; shunchaki SMS yozishingiz mumkin. Ba'zan odamlar bunga juda ishonib qolishadi va yuzma-yuz gaplashishni unutishadi.
questions.uzSampleBand7: Mobil telefonlar, shubhasiz, aloqani inqilob qildi. Hozir kim bilandir, qayerda bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, bog'lanish juda oson. Biz elektron pochta, SMS yuborishimiz yoki video qo'ng'iroq qilishimiz mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bu yuzma-yuz muloqotning pasayishiga ham olib keldi, bu esa haqiqiy achinarli holat. Odamlar ba'zan shaxsan muloqot qilishni unutishadi.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Xo'sh, mobil telefonlar aloqa qilish usulimizni tubdan o'zgartirdi. Bu, albatta, aloqani yanada qulay va tezkor qildi. Biz odamlarni dunyoning deyarli istalgan joyida bir zumda topishimiz mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bu faqat qo'ng'iroqlar haqida emas; bizda ijtimoiy tarmoqlar, xabar almashish ilovalari va video konferentsiyalar mavjud. Biroq, aloqa qilishning bu qulayligi ham o'z kamchiliklariga ega, bu esa o'zaro munosabatlarimizda chuqurlik etishmasligiga olib kelishi mumkin, deb o'ylayman.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Mobil telefonlar shubhasiz aloqani o'zgartirib, giper-bog'langan dunyoni yaratdi. Ularning taqdim etayotgan tezkorligi va qulayligi misli ko'rilmagan; biz istalgan vaqtda, istalgan joyda, istalgan odam bilan bog'lana olamiz. Bu global hamkorlikni rivojlantirdi va to'siqlarni olib tashladi. Bundan tashqari, aloqa usullarining xilma-xilligi - tezkor xabarlardan tortib video qo'ng'iroqlargacha - hayratlanarli. Biroq, bu doimiy bog'liqlik ikki tomonlama qilich bo'lishi mumkin, bu esa yuzaki munosabatlarga va ish bilan shaxsiy hayot o'rtasidagi chegaralarning xiralashishiga olib kelishi mumkin; biz muvozanatni saqlashimiz kerak, deb o'ylayman.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Mobil telefonlar—va ayniqsa smartfonlar—aloqani shunchalik keng qamrovli tarzda o'zgartirdiki, hozir ularsiz aloqa qanday bo'lganini eslash qiyin. Eng tub o'zgarish, ehtimol, sinxron aloqadan asinxron aloqaga o'tish bo'ldi—mobil telefonlardan oldin aloqaning aksariyati yuzma-yuz yoki telefon orqali bo'lar edi, bu esa ikkala tomonning ham bir vaqtda mavjud bo'lishini talab qiladi. Xabar almashish darhol javob berishni talab qilmaydigan tarzda aloqa qilishni odatiy holga aylantirdi, bu esa afzalliklarga ham ega—siz o'z tezligingizda, vaqt zonalarida, qilayotgan ishingizni to'xtatmasdan aloqa qilishingiz mumkin—va kamchiliklarga ham ega—mavjud bo'lish umidlari kamayish o'rniga ko'proq oshdi va ko'p odamlar tezda javob berish bosimini his qilishadi, bu chinakam stressli bo'lishi mumkin. Mavjud aloqa usullarining xilma-xilligi ham keskin kengaydi—matn, ovoz, video, rasm va emoji barchasi turli xil kommunikativ vazifalarni bajaradi va ifodaning yangi shakllarini yaratdi. Menimcha, eng muhim o'zgarishlardan biri bu ommaviy va shaxsiy aloqa o'rtasidagi chegaraning xiralashishi—xabarlarni baham ko'rish, yo'naltirish va translyatsiya qilish qulayligi shaxsiy suhbat tabiatini ishonch va yaqinlik uchun muhim oqibatlarga olib keladigan tarzda o'zgartirdi. Raqamli aloqaning doimiyligi—xabarlarni saqlash, qidirish va olish mumkinligi—og'zaki suhbatning vaqtinchalik tabiatidan ham sezilarli farq qiladi.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages and disadvantages of mobile phones for elderly people?

vocabulary.title: Q17 - Phones for Elderly People
phrases: direct link to family and emergency services
see as well as hear family members
didn't grow up with digital technology
sentenceStarters: Mobile phones offer significant potential benefits for elderly people...
The most significant advantage is probably safety and connection...
The disadvantages are also real...

questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I think mobile phones, they can help old people. But, um, it's a bit difficult to learn. Maybe it is good for emergencies, but also, uh, expensive. They can get confused. So, yeah, good and bad.
questions.sampleBand6: I think there are definitely some advantages and disadvantages. Obviously, it's great for them to keep in touch with family. But, um, some elderly people might find the technology a bit overwhelming. And, another thing is, they might be more vulnerable to scams, so that's a real concern, I think.
questions.sampleBand7: Well, mobile phones can be really beneficial for elderly people, particularly in terms of staying connected with family and friends. It offers them a sense of security, knowing they can get in touch with someone in an emergency. However, there's also the risk of them falling victim to online scams, and the complexity of some devices can be quite daunting for them. So, it's a mixed bag, really.
questions.sampleBand8: From my perspective, mobile phones present both opportunities and challenges for elderly individuals. On the one hand, they offer a vital lifeline for maintaining social connections and accessing essential services. They can reach out to family, order groceries, or even access telehealth services. Moreover, they provide a sense of independence and security. However, the disadvantages include the potential for social isolation if they become overly reliant on their phones, and the increased vulnerability to online fraud and scams. It's a double-edged sword, I'd say.
questions.sampleBand9: Well, it's a multifaceted issue. Mobile phones can be incredibly empowering for elderly people, allowing them to maintain their independence and social lives. They can effortlessly keep up with family members, access vital information, and even participate in online communities. In an emergency, they offer an immediate sense of security. However, there's also a darker side. Many elderly individuals struggle with the technology itself, which can lead to frustration and a feeling of being left behind. Furthermore, they are often easy targets for scams and online fraud, and this can have devastating consequences. So, while the potential benefits are substantial, careful consideration and support are essential to iron out the potential pitfalls.
questions.sampleAnswer: Mobile phones offer significant potential benefits for elderly people, but also present genuine challenges, and I think the balance between benefits and challenges varies considerably depending on the individual and the level of support available to them. The most significant advantage is probably safety and connection—for elderly people living alone, a mobile phone provides a direct link to family, friends, and emergency services that can be genuinely life-saving. The ability to call for help in an emergency, to stay in contact with family members, and to access information and services remotely has real and significant value. Video calling in particular has been transformative for many elderly people—the ability to see as well as hear family members who live at a distance has reduced the isolation that can be a significant problem in later life. The disadvantages are also real—the complexity of modern smartphones can be genuinely daunting for people who didn't grow up with digital technology, and the pace of change means that interfaces and apps are constantly evolving in ways that require continuous learning. The risk of fraud and scams is also disproportionately high for elderly users, who are often specifically targeted by criminals. I think the most important thing is to ensure that elderly people have access to the support and training they need to use phones safely and effectively, and that phone design takes the needs of older users seriously rather than treating them as an afterthought.
questions.uzSampleBand5: Xo'sh, mm, o'ylaymanki, mobil telefonlar qariyalarga yordam berishi mumkin. Lekin, mm, buni o'rganish biroz qiyin. Ehtimol, favqulodda vaziyatlar uchun yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin, lekin, yana, uh, qimmat ham. Ularning boshi qotishi mumkin. Xullas, ha, yaxshi ham, yomon ham.

questions.uzSampleBand7: Xo'sh, mobil telefonlar keksa odamlar uchun juda foydali bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa oila va do'stlar bilan aloqada bo'lish nuqtai nazaridan. Bu ularga xavfsizlik hissini beradi, chunki ular favqulodda vaziyatda kim bilandir bog'lanishlari mumkinligini bilishadi. Biroq, ularning onlayn firibgarlik qurboni bo'lishi xavfi ham bor va ba'zi qurilmalarning murakkabligi ular uchun juda qo'rqinchli bo'lishi mumkin. Shunday ekan, bu aralash holat, aslida.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Mening nuqtai nazarimga ko'ra, mobil telefonlar keksa odamlar uchun ham imkoniyatlar, ham qiyinchiliklarni taqdim etadi. Bir tomondan, ular ijtimoiy aloqalarni saqlab qolish va muhim xizmatlardan foydalanish uchun hayotiy muhim imkoniyatni taklif qiladi. Ular oilasiga qo'ng'iroq qila oladi, oziq-ovqat buyurtma qilishi yoki hatto tele-salomatlik xizmatlaridan foydalanishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ular mustaqillik va xavfsizlik hissini ta'minlaydi. Biroq, kamchiliklarga, agar ular telefonlariga haddan tashqari bog'lanib qolsalar, ijtimoiy izolyatsiya ehtimoli va onlayn firibgarlik va aldashga nisbatan zaiflikning oshishi kiradi. Bu, men aytardimki, ikki tomonlama qilich.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Xo'sh, bu ko'p qirrali masala. Mobil telefonlar keksa odamlar uchun juda kuchli bo'lishi mumkin, bu ularga mustaqillik va ijtimoiy hayotlarini saqlab qolish imkonini beradi. Ular oila a'zolari bilan osonlikcha aloqada bo'lishi, muhim ma'lumotlarga kirish va hatto onlayn hamjamiyatlarda ishtirok etishi mumkin. Favqulodda vaziyatda ular darhol xavfsizlik hissini taqdim etadi. Biroq, uning qorong'u tomoni ham bor. Ko'pgina keksa odamlar texnologiyaning o'zi bilan kurashadilar, bu esa umidsizlikka va ortda qolish hissi paydo bo'lishiga olib kelishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ular ko'pincha firibgarlik va onlayn aldash uchun oson nishonlar, va bu halokatli oqibatlarga olib kelishi mumkin. Shunday ekan, potentsial foyda katta bo'lsa-da, potentsial kamchiliklarni bartaraf etish uchun ehtiyotkorlik bilan ko'rib chiqish va qo'llab-quvvatlash muhimdir.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Mobil telefonlar keksa odamlar uchun sezilarli darajada foyda keltirishi mumkin, lekin haqiqiy qiyinchiliklarni ham tug'diradi, va menimcha, foyda va qiyinchiliklar o'rtasidagi muvozanat individual shaxsga va ularga mavjud bo'lgan yordam darajasiga qarab sezilarli darajada farq qiladi. Eng muhim afzalligi, ehtimol, xavfsizlik va aloqadir — yolg'iz yashaydigan keksa odamlar uchun mobil telefon oila, do'stlar va favqulodda xizmatlar bilan to'g'ridan-to'g'ri aloqani ta'minlaydi, bu haqiqatan ham hayotni saqlab qolishi mumkin. Favqulodda vaziyatda yordam so'rash, oila a'zolari bilan aloqada bo'lish va masofadan turib ma'lumot va xizmatlardan foydalanish imkoniyati haqiqiy va muhim ahamiyatga ega. Ayniqsa, video qo'ng'iroqlar ko'plab keksa odamlar uchun o'zgarishlar yasadi — uzoqda yashaydigan oila a'zolarini eshitish bilan birga ko'rish imkoniyati keyingi hayotda muhim muammo bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan izolyatsiyani kamaytirdi. Kamchiliklari ham haqiqiy — zamonaviy smartfonlarning murakkabligi raqamli texnologiyalar bilan o'smagan odamlar uchun juda qiyin bo'lishi mumkin, o'zgarish sur'ati esa interfeyslar va ilovalar doimiy ravishda o'zgarib turishini anglatadi, bu doimiy o'rganishni talab qiladi. Firibgarlik va aldash xavfi ham keksa foydalanuvchilar uchun nomutanosib ravishda yuqori, ular ko'pincha jinoyatchilar tomonidan maqsadli ravishda nishonga olinadi. Menimcha, eng muhim narsa shundaki, keksa odamlarning telefonlardan xavfsiz va samarali foydalanish uchun zarur bo'lgan yordam va treningga ega bo'lishini ta'minlash kerak va telefon dizayni ularni shunchaki keyingi o'rinda turuvchi narsa sifatida qaramasdan, keksa foydalanuvchilarning ehtiyojlarini jiddiy qabul qilishi kerak.
